issue_context.summary: After updating to PowerToys 0.101.2373 Preview from the Microsoft Store, Command Palette Dock still appears and auto-hides but renders no system information or shortcuts.
known_information: Affected module is Command Palette Dock on Windows 10 x64.
The issue was observed after an update and the Dock bar still appears/auto-hides.
Expected Dock content includes system information on the right and shortcuts on the left; actual content is blank.
Restarting, deleting a PowerToys Run JSON file, restarting Explorer, and running as administrator did not resolve it.
The reporter supplied a screenshot and a fresh PowerToysReport ZIP after the /bugreport request.
The latest comment asks about reinstalling and configuration backup/restore, without confirming a new test result.
inferences: The Dock window creation and auto-hide path likely succeeds while content initialization or state restoration may be failing.
Deleting the PowerToys Run JSON file does not test Dock state because Dock belongs to Command Palette.
The exact failing branch cannot be distinguished from the public report without maintainer reproduction and inspection of the supplied diagnostic archive.
issue_context.analysis: The report now contains enough evidence for a focused maintainer reproduction and report inspection, so another generic log request would duplicate work. A concrete reproduction action is appropriate while the fix assessment remains not_applicable until the failing initialization path is confirmed.

reproduce.title: Verify Command Palette Dock content after update
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.101.2373 Preview or current development build on Windows 10 x64
prerequisites: Always-on-top or equivalent Dock setting available
A Windows 10 x64 test environment with the affected update path
The reporter-provided PowerToysReport ZIP available for comparison
steps: Start from a clean PowerToys launch on Windows 10 x64 and open Command Palette Dock.
Verify whether the Dock bar appears and auto-hides.
Check whether the expected system-information area and shortcut area populate.
Repeat after restarting PowerToys and Explorer; do not delete PowerToys Run state as a substitute for Dock state.
If the bar remains blank, inspect the supplied PowerToysReport archive and capture the first initialization/state-restoration failure.
If the content populates, compare the persisted Dock settings and update/migration state with the supplied report.
reproduce.expected_result: The Dock displays its system information and shortcuts while retaining the reported auto-hide behavior; if it remains blank, the failing initialization transition and diagnostic evidence are identified for a targeted design.
setup_requirements: Record the exact Windows build, install scope, and current PowerToys build.
Use the attached report ZIP rather than requesting a duplicate /bugreport unless the reproduction produces materially different evidence.

upstream_safety.detail: No public mutation was made to microsoft/PowerToys.
